en: An amorphous, sticky monster found everywhere. It favors damp places, clinging to prey and trying to digest it with its whole body. Still, barring something truly unusual, it is unlikely to put your life in danger.
A mysterious thing sighted in many lands. It is round and cute, so some poke it with a finger for fun, but it resists spells well and fights back a fair bit, so be careful.

A slime said to be dyed red with the blood of adventurers... In truth, it is a slime discolored by differences in the soil. Adapted to survive harsher environments, it is stronger than a Slime, but in the end, it is just a slime.

A creature rising from the ground, stalking prey with a formless body and big eyes. Its thick tentacles are surprisingly strong and reach even the back row, so low-level Mages and such often fall prey. If it looks dangerous, have the front row cover them.

Life that dwells inside a flask, born of the secret arts of alchemy. The vast magic poured into it lets it float, flask and all. Perhaps to protect itself, it attacks even from inside the flask with a strange power called Psi Blade.
Mere clay set in motion by high-level magic. Fiercely loyal to its maker, it is said never to disobey. For that reason, frail mages sometimes keep one at their side as a bodyguard.

A magical creature that takes in all kinds of living things and grows ever larger, keeping its shape. Some of its victims bond with the Jellita and fuse with it instead of being digested. Touch it bare and digestion starts right there, so armor is a must.

A monster with a lion's face and many beastly legs. It looks like nothing but someone's bad joke. Its many legs let it move at frightening speed, but adventurers whisper, "Sure, it's fast side to side, but isn't it slow going forward and back?"

If a vine coils around you with unreasonable strength as you walk in the forest, it may be a Weird Kelp. Leave it be and it will slowly wrap you up and drag you into a pitcher made of leaves and brimming with digestive juices.
Plump, sexy lips. A tongue writhing in the mouth, bewitchingly wet. A cute snaggletooth peeking out. Anyone's heart would be stolen... if only they were attached to a human body.

A tycoon of old built a piggy bank that dodges danger on its own so no one could steal the fortune: the Goggle Eye. But who could have guessed it would flee from its owner too? The owner seems long gone, so let's gratefully claim what's inside.

A knight living in a canvas. What it is after is unknown, but it will see most adventurers as enemies and attack them. It uses no special attacks, so if they surround you, stay calm and burn them away.

A wild beast living in a canvas. Perhaps bored inside the painting, it attacks anyone passing nearby without discrimination. It has no notable traits, so as long as you handle it correctly, it should not be that tough a foe.

A mechanical bird. Its ferocity and machine precision torment adventurers. Yet turn that precision against it and you'll run rings around it. Perhaps they look alike: now and then one mistakes a rooftop weathercock for a female of its kind and courts it.
Living armor. It poses as an ornament, then suddenly attacks. It may be empty inside, but it carries a full set of knight's gear, so don't let your guard down.

Also called the Void Hound. An otherworldly monster said to live by devouring space. Why the Edumo exist is unknown. One theory says they dispose of unneeded space by eating it, and will come in packs when the gods decide the end of the world.

Every adventurer knows slimes, but in fact little research has been done on their ecology. A slime's lifespan is also unknown, and at times you may meet a giant slime that seems centuries old. Its size is startling at first, but a slime is still a slime.

A bizarre creature that feeds on carrion. The sight of Rags swarming over an adventurer left out in the open is truly revolting. They rarely come down to human settlements, but if civilians ever saw one, it would cause quite a stir.

A nasty foe that nests in treasure chests and waits for adventurers. Even at high levels, its "Miasma Wave" can halve your HP, so take care. But how do Thieves remove a Mimic's trap? Perhaps it is a creature like a hermit crab.

A monster of many theories: a warrior trapped in a twisted world, a discarded failed Homunculus out for revenge, a dream demon's minion, a soldier from another dimension. Its form is so shocking, they say, that onlookers dream of it or go mad on the spot.

A further-grown Homunculus. Save for its head, its body no longer crumbles in open air. Crack its head flask a little and the protective fluid spills; it soon dies. But if they are made on a whim and killed for no real reason, do their lives mean anything?

An Edumo Senior is an Edumo of proven power and record, granted some free will and allowed to act on it. Acting on their own, some reportedly interact with those who dwell on the land and achieve their own inner growth.

For those who wield magic, the Tetramystica is the finest defensive token. It is far harder to build than a golem, but once built it is said to be worth an army of ten thousand. It often outlives its master, and in such cases is said to gain free will.
The corpses of those who collapsed and died in the labyrinth, or of unlucky souls killed by monsters and left to rot, risen and walking. Take care not to join their ranks.
A skeleton set in motion by someone's curse. Normally, the monsters called undead have no memories of their life. But on rare occasions, one keeps part of its former memories.

A demon that feeds on carrion. No wonder they love to settle in labyrinths: they are littered with dead adventurers. Then again, perhaps one day you yourselves will give in to hunger and become Ghouls.

A zombie dog. Humans have so much needless wisdom that turning zombie seems to strip them of everything, but those with little intellect to begin with act much as they did in life. Zombie Fangs are no exception: they're said to gnaw Skeleton bones for fun.
The corpse of a samurai carrying the famed blade Hundred Bamboo Edge. Some attack him to get the sword, but many are said to have been cut down in turn. Is that power truly his own, or the sword's?

A Bass Dragon turned zombie. Mid-level adventurers sometimes fish in dungeons as one way to find food. But reeling in a Bass Zombi is a letdown. Would a revival spell bring its fish meat back to life?

A woman who died in childbirth or grieving a stillbirth is said to become a Langsuir. With a mouth on the back of her head she drinks blood and, perhaps from regret, preys only on children. Killing another's child won't bring hers back. Surely she knows...

The very byword for those who live in darkness. Vampires come in several ranks, and these are the lowest. Even so, ordinary adventurers must be wary of them. If the Priest's drain barrier spell has worn off, fleeing is also the right call.

A bizarre tree said to grow in the world of darkness. It latches onto the bodies of sinners and drops its fruit into their mouths. The fruit is terribly bitter, but there is no escaping the Zaqqum; they are said to be force-fed it endlessly.

A knight that symbolizes death. It does not come to deal death; it is a monster that visits those whose death draws near. Though undead, it is closer to a fairy. To defeat a Dullahan is also to overcome your own fated death. Steel yourself!

Giants with an element of their own are close to spirits, and on death they rarely leave a corpse, returning straight to nature. But some giants are far from spirits, and such louts end up as zombies. If you meet one, beat it to a pulp to lay it to rest.

An undead noble who gained the power of darkness. Even as its body rots away, the magic and dignity within it never fade. It saps your party's strength to add to its servants, so finish it off quickly when you meet one.
A skeleton warrior bearing a great scythe. If your front row's defense is thin, it will easily take their heads. If you can't handle it, Dispel is an option too.

A burly Skeleton infused with power, so big it is little different from a giant. Many Skeletons go into it, so when a Girou is smashed, the shards return to Skeleton form. After a Girou falls, vast numbers of Skeletons are said to lie strewn about.

Curse or obsession? It is an undead dragon, a creature called the mightiest on earth. Even its breath has changed and its form is long gone, yet you still sense its majesty. But you are alive. Dragon or not, you can't let the dead reap your lives. Fight!

A knight of the underworld. To guard persons of importance, it stands before you without expression and calmly does its duty. Its otherworldly blows, if poorly blocked, will deal heavy damage to the party.

A child of human and vampire blood. Most die soon after birth, so adult Dhampirs are very rare. Perhaps due to their vampire blood, they can sense vampires. Many are persecuted for their mixed blood, and their natures vary widely.

A vampiress whose bewitching beauty ensnares prey, young women above all. Unlike rough lesser vampires, she draws her victim close by the waist, speaks of love, and waits till their eyes melt with bliss. Those charmed by her sweet kiss offer their blood.

A sharp scythe that reaps heads in one sweep, a skull foretelling death, a vile centipede's body. You freeze, and suddenly every ally but you is dead... with this monster, that's commonplace. If you meet one, curse yourself for wandering into such a place.

One who reigns at the very top of the undead, also called a True Ancestor. With vast magic and many minions, it keeps lowly adventurers at bay. Even if you get in close, its sharp fangs are hard to fend off. Do mind your manners.

One of the four great elements of all things: the elemental of earth. Spirits are not harmful, but act by their own laws, so you may offend one unknowingly. It is not that strong, but if one attacks you, pay close attention to why it did.
A dwarf fairy living in the forest. It loves to dance, and draws passing travelers into its dancing ring, making them dance until they drop. When alone, however, it turns extremely timid.

A spirit dwelling in a tree. It takes a womanly form, and it is said those pure of heart can befriend it. It usually lives quietly in the forest, but if anyone ravages the forest, it binds them with its vines.
One of the four great elements of all things: the elemental of water. A spirit found everywhere; those who can feel the mystical close at hand are said to be able to find it in any place.

Fairy folk and spirits, with the Fairy as the best-known example, are at root a system that keeps the land's magic flowing. So although they do have personalities, to humans and others they come across as very aloof.

A water sprite known alongside the Water Elemental. Beautiful in form, modest and very gentle by nature. They often fall in love with humans or elves, but betray their devotion and the water clan will use every means at hand to come for revenge.

A mountain fairy who grows turnips. It hands out turnip and radish seeds to children but is unwelcome, so it is always grumpy. Its sack, naturally, holds turnip seeds, radish seeds and such. Its hobby is strolling about counting the turnips it has grown.

One of the four great elements of all things: the elemental of wind. As if to say "nothing in this world stays the same," it keeps changing the land. Yet even a wind spirit stops now and then. If the wind suddenly dies on an adventure, one may be near.

Trees that live for many years merge with spirits and gain a will of their own. Treants are one such kind. Usually silent, they sometimes speak to elves or gnomes when a great calamity or change is coming.

One of the four great elements of all things: the elemental of fire. Fire at times warms body and soul, at times burns all to ash. When gratitude and awe for fire are forgotten, the Fire Elemental turns into a purging flame.

A monster born when snow, rounded up like a rabbit, came to life. It is gentle by nature, but when it senses danger it unleashes the magic hidden inside and launches merciless attacks. Be on your guard when a pack of them attacks.

A wind spirit. It flits round and round, carrying breezes everywhere. It is free-spirited by nature and hurls vacuum blades when in a foul mood. They say if it takes a liking to you, it carries you off in a whirlwind and you can never come back.

A fairy said to know where gold, silver and treasure lie. It looks stubborn, but rumor says it is a timid elder. Also a shoemaker, it makes shoes for every race from fairies to giants. When a traveler's shoes break, it seems to pop up and mend them.

It appears before you out of nowhere. Speak and it won't answer; stare and you can't make out its form. A higher being's fragment, a demon in a god's guise, mere weather... Many tales are told, but lately some whisper it may be "a warning of some kind."

A strange light drifting in many places, also called a ghost light. Reach for it carelessly and the strange waves from its glowing body will freeze you in place. Its stamina is modest, but neither magic nor physical attacks work well on it: a tough foe.

An elemental that rules darkness. It moves through shadows, wandering in search of deeper dark. Being kin to the spirits, it is normally very docile, but the miasma of evil can drive it to attack people. If you see one, you would do well to keep away.
A bewitching flower that blooms in deep forests. It moves its leaves and vines at will to entangle travelers it takes a fancy to. Any poor adventurer it catches will be digested as nourishment.

A lovely woman of the snowy peaks, with translucent white skin and a bewitching smile. Cold inside too, her breath never turns white: that's how to tell her from a normal woman. Rumors range from her killing the lost in the snow to her marrying for love.

Surly and aggressive, they're often taken for fairies gone astray, but far from it. They have merely come closer to a fairy's true nature than ordinary ones. To fulfill their duty as a mana-circulation system, they attack to release the power within you.

Legend says a carefully made snowman gains a heart and helps mind children until it melts in spring. But if its heart goes unnoticed and it is neglected, loneliness draws an evil will, and it becomes a fiend freezing children to keep them by it forever.

A fire djinn that freely commands all flame. The air around it is always searing; an Ifrit's mere arrival sets the area ablaze. Unskilled summoners who make a pact beyond their means are often engulfed in flames and burned to ash the moment they call it.

A spirit that rules all four great elements of all things. A union of fire, water, earth and wind, it embodies the balance of magic that dwells in the world. When that balance breaks, it is said to appear to restore the world to its rightful form.
Its hard shell can't be cracked even with a hammer, and its sharp claws tear flesh with ease. It watches for an opening, then pounces, so if you don't judge your distance carefully, you'll be sorry.
A mosquito with a mouth as sharp as a pike, the spear soldiers carry. It's only a mosquito, so it's no great foe, but lose enough blood and you'll still die. Be careful when a swarm surrounds you.

It turns the floor into quicksand to drag adventurers down to itself. With their formation broken, adventurers may be wiped out without being able to do a thing. If you run into one, take it out first.

Its most striking feature is a pair of huge scythes for arms, over 2 m long. The scythes cut better than a long sword and can even behead. It is feared not only by adventurers but by insect monsters too.

It gapes its crooked-toothed mouth like an idiot. Its supple tentacles can wrap around a foe in an instant, crush every bone and swallow it whole, head first. Even if you're lucky enough to dodge, your gear will likely be destroyed.

It scurries about at outrageous speed, dodging attacks and calling in swarms of its kin. More of them won't put the party in danger, but a battle that never ends is torture. Just do the sensible thing and burn them away with magic.

A fearsome coconut crab. In the forest it comes at you openly, snapping branches as it goes. Slow but hard to stop, it is very dangerous when several surround you. It has instinctive cunning too, good at driving prey into dead ends, so handle it with care.

A scorpion monster found mainly in deserts. When an already dangerous creature mutates into a monster, its danger is beyond measure. When the venomous tail comes flying, the front row should brace their shields.

A giant centipede that coils around a shield and lives in it like a hermit crab. Its defense is already tough, yet it hardens its allies further with spells. Some adventurers mistake the centipede for the shield's decoration and pay dearly for it.

Cordyceps are fungi that take over larvae in the soil; the true body is the plant part. But in this rare cordyceps the host also lives on in symbiosis. The flower gathers the tiny flying bugs that serve as food, and the insect preys on them.

Not content with scurrying, they now even fly. The terror of having one leap at you is beyond imagining. They have nests, which you may find on your adventures. If so, the wise move is to leave quietly. Poke one for fun, and a black terror will engulf you.

A strange creature that seizes prey with two oddly shaped jaws. The accordion-like, arm-shaped upper jaw is stronger than it looks; once it gets a firm grip, even a human can hardly escape. If you hear a grating "bzzzt," you had best be on your guard.

A mighty queen bee. It often rules a corner of the forest and shows no mercy to those who run wild in its territory, so take care not to upset it. Being a bee, it adores nectar; at harvest time it is seen flying about merrily in search of flowers itself.

A giant poison moth monster. A single beat of its wings fills the area with a deadly toxic miasma. It waits for its poisoned prey to weaken bit by bit, then, once they can no longer move, drives its needle-like mouth into the nape of their neck.

King of the flies, the VIP of the insect world. It sits on a throne and has its fly subjects pull it. These flies are called "fly knights" and are fiercely loyal. To protect their lord, it is said they think nothing of their own lives.

They live in flocks in dark, cramped places, always hunting for prey by ultrasound. Once they find it, they fly straight in and go for the base of the neck with fang and claw. They prefer blood to flesh, hence the name 'Vampire.'

Rats that fed on the flesh and blood of dead adventurers. More aggressive than ordinary rats and a size bigger. They know how adventurers taste, so if their cute looks lure you closer, they'll bite without mercy.

Its warty skin is coated in poison that leaves anyone who touches it Poisoned. It's surprisingly strong, too: if its kick lands in your gut, you'll double over. If you can remove the poisonous parts, its meat is edible.
A ray-like animal that drifts and flutters through the air. It is surprisingly quick, and its habit of attacking twice at once is a nuisance. Then again, that's all it is.

A bird known for its chunky body and lovable face. Its wings are too small to fly, but instead it gained legs to run on the ground. Its lower-body muscles are so developed it is round all over, hence the name meat bomb. Its meat is muscly, so tastes vary.

A monster known for its burly body and long, sharp horn. As a rule it doesn't attack other creatures, but once it's worked up, that's another story. With a burst of speed and a piercing charge, it kills foes in the blink of an eye.

A mountain bear. It lives quietly far from towns, and leaves to avoid a fight when it hears adventurers' footsteps. But when food runs short, hunger drives it down to the foothills. Most sightings are of these hungry bears, hence its fierce reputation.

The Ripper Mizuchi is the bane of fishermen and sailors. Its whole body is covered in sword-sharp blades that shred the nets they set. But if you meet one, worry about your own skin, not your tools of the trade.

An odd animal that walks on its nose, balancing with its tail. Standing, it reaches a person's waist; its body is surprisingly big. It is docile, but when angered it casts the spell Zeo Nadar. If you meet a group of them, why not settle things peacefully?

A huge creature, part man and part ape, met on snowy mountains. It's often seen, but no one has settled whether it is an animal, a near-human or a spirit. In a world where spirits and spells are commonplace, half-baked mysteries like it tend to be ignored.

It swallows prey, water and all, with its huge mouth. It lives in dark, cold places and rises to the surface only to feed. It is so ferocious it bears the name 'Dragon.' Then again, real dragons are rather intelligent, so they may find that a nuisance.

Also called the Silver Hunter. It races across snowfields like a gale, cleverly drives its prey into its hunting ground, pins it down and kills it. It usually acts alone, but in packs they can even bring down foes above their level.

A sheep that has gained magical power. It has a strong spell barrier of its own and tries to lower its foes' spell resistance. When it shows up with mages or monsters that cast evasion-raising spells, it becomes a real pain.

A giant ape with several arms. You would expect brilliant combination attacks from them, but each arm seems to move on its own whims, with no coordination at all. Even mid-battle, its spare arms pick its nose or hold food, doing as they please.

The slimy mucus covering its body makes weapons slip off. It stores foul, pitch-black ink and spits it at foes when in danger. The smell is hard to wash out and saps morale on its own, but it is actually delicious: one of the Three Great Delicacies.

It cuts foes in two, bone and all, with its huge pincers and spits foamy digestive juice. Despite the name, it has nothing to do with ogres, except that an odd ogre puts one in a stew. Its tomalley is one of Hestrio's Three Great Delicacies. Remember that.

In the pitch-black world of the deep sea, the vivid fins it suddenly spreads catch the eye. But this is nothing less than a declaration of war. It circles you seeking an opening to attack, yet carefree adventurers keep mistaking it for a welcome.

A beast, just as the name says. Savage and aggressive, dim and rash, rude and ungrateful. You wouldn't want it as an enemy, of course, or even by your side as an ally. Yet it seems every rule has exceptions: some women reportedly like the Beast type.

A giant flying whale. It feeds by inhaling 'something' in the air, with suction so strong that, if unlucky, even an adult gets sucked in. Its size will knock you off your feet, but there is said to be a giant bird, the Wargle, that preys on Airy Viders.

Tyrant of the forest: a menace that runs about on its huge body, mowing down trees. It needs a long run-up to start "running," but then won't stop, and is fairly fast. Meet one while camping and there's no time to save your gear: beat it or lose your gear.

Emperor Birds are very intelligent and once had fairly friendly ties with people. But since their delicious eggs were hailed as one of the Three Great Delicacies, endless overhunting has soured relations. Their bonds are strong; a long fight is dangerous.

It moves among the trees like the wind, too swift to ever be seen. It toys with adventurers with shifting attacks that could come from any side. A front row that senses trouble and turns around may well find the back row soaked in blood.
A giant bird monster with the head and breasts of a human woman. Usually they attack adventurers for their food, but in breeding season they may attack for another purpose.

A miraculous mythical beast that always shields the gem in its forehead with both paws. A Carbuncle's gem gives off its own light and has the power to drive away darkness. Large ones can fetch high prices, so adventurers often chase them down.

You walk up thinking it's a bat, but it's a giant eyeball... that's an Eye Wing. Perhaps because of its huge eye, it tends to shun bright, dazzling places. It's no great threat, but its poison spells are a nuisance. Watch out when they come in groups.

A lizard full of poison. If its claws merely graze you, venom seeps in and eats at your whole body. Keep your distance, then? When its claws can't reach, a Basilisk attacks with deadly poison breath. After the fight, you'll surely be drenched in poison.

A monstrous bird that looks like a deer and a bird combined. For some reason a peryton's shadow is human-shaped, and killing a person lets it regain its own shadow, so it is said to seek out and attack humans.

It takes the form of a winged serpent, and in some lands is revered as a messenger of the gods, or as a god itself. It swoops down from the sky without warning, so let your guard down and it will catch you napping.

A heavenly steed said to open its heart only to the pure. Like the horn on its brow, it favors those who devote themselves single-mindedly to one thing. If you want to befriend a unicorn, you had better not keep changing class on a whim.

"Oh my, a lion in the sea? But lo and behold, its lower half's a fish! Holy mackerel!?" A monster striking enough to excuse such fishermen's babble. It is fairly smart and famously tidy. If you don't want to anger it, don't throw garbage into the sea.

A monster fused from several animals. Each of its three heads attacks in its own way: the dragon with breath, the ox with spells, the lion with matchless fangs. Beating a Chimera is what separates novices from intermediate adventurers.

Glittering wings and a gorgeous crest: a lavish mythical beast, yet it cannot fly. But who needs flight with an inborn power to petrify? Not just its attacks but its breath can turn you to stone. Take it lightly and you'll be a stone statue in no time.

A monster that is part aged human, part magical beast. It understands human speech and is very clever. At times it speaks kindly to weary adventurers, coaxing them to give up. Facing a Manticore may test your resolve more than your strength.

A demon beast writhing slickly amid water columns. With an allure only inhuman women have, it draws adventurers in, off guard, though they know it's a monster. Supple, mighty tentacles snare them, and the fanged lower mouth, not the upper, swallows them.

A monster famed as the "Hound of Hell." Its eerie, red-glowing eyes drive absolute terror into all who face it, rooting them to the spot. Do the denizens of darkness all keep such vicious beasts as pets?

A noble, deeply loyal mythical beast said to let only those whose strength it acknowledges ride on its back. It is sung that one who rides a griffon will rule the land, and many put its image on flags and crests, hoping to borrow a griffon's power.

A beauty with a snake's body. Intelligent, she seldom attacks people, but things like 'magic pools' can make her drunk and violent. Rumor says a child born of love with a Lamia will have rare magic and be able to command every mythical beast.

A sacred bird whose lifeblood is said to grant eternal life. Born in raging flames, it carries flame within, so it is hard to approach. Come near it carelessly for its blood, and that rash act will be atoned for in purging fire.

A fox that lived long and gained mystic powers. Some take human form to beguile the powerful; others shun people in tiny mountain shrines. Angered, it calls heavenly winds and black clouds and strikes with eerie lightning. Proud, but fried tofu undoes it.
A fearsome beast that would easily spawn a legend or two if it ever came to the surface. The blows of its giant body are all it has, but the simpler the attack, the less you can take it lightly.
Queen of the Phoenixes, at the summit of the fire spirits. The flames the Phoenix Queen wears burn far hotter than a Phoenix's; they say that when she is angry, even Phoenixes are burned to death.

A divine sea fish shining with holy light. Any beast this huge should be slow, yet maybe thanks to the light magic it wears, it races about at baffling speed. So adventurers keep dying, unable to keep their distance or thrown off their usual rhythm.

A mythical beast long known as a symbol of intellect. When it finds adventurers, it poses puzzles called riddles. Those who can satisfy the sphinx's thirst for knowledge may be able to build a good relationship with it.

A spirit of the dead, so to speak. It is a mere soul, so there's no need to mind it. But if you do mean to banish it, most weapons pass right through, so bring a Priest who can strike spirits, or a suitable weapon.
A malicious, dangerous soul. It trails the adventurer it has marked, waiting for a chance to drag them into the afterlife. It's hard to hit with weapons, so if it looks dangerous, rely on Dispel.

A ghost that loves pranks, from cute ones like flying plates or doors that open and shut, to dangerous ones like flying weapons and blades. Sometimes it wants someone to notice something, so if you scold it and hear it out, you might become friends.

The spirit of a warrior who fights on even after falling. It is as strong as in life, but just being a spirit makes it a very troublesome foe. Take it out with spells and the like before it makes you one of its own.
The ghost of a sorcerer. A sorcerer alone is a dangerous foe early in the game, and with physical attacks not working on it either, it is a real menace.

The ghost of a female adventurer who lost her companions on a journey and died alone. If you sense someone in the labyrinth and call out, and the same words come back, it's probably an Echo. Head toward the voice, and you'll become her new companion.
A pesky spirit that can't give up thieving even in death. This otherworldly thief is after not your valuables, but the souls of adventurers.

She who heralds death. People think "the Banshee brings death," but Banshees only appear where death is. They shed every tear to comfort fading lives. Classed as ghosts, they are really closer to spirits. Pray their tears are not meant for you.

A spirit that hangs upside down from the ceiling; who knows what fun it finds in that. The sight of them all dropping from above at once is oddly moving, in its way. Take care not to be startled into letting them strike first.

A lost nun. She gave her life to the gods, so why does she wander this world in death like this? You may wish to reach her heart, but the gaze she turns on you is empty. At the very least, give her your blessing so she can rest in peace.

Novice servants forever make clumsy blunders. Fine if you can laugh it off, but some cost a life. The Ghost Maid is one such soul. Unaware she died, she still busily cleans for her master. Rumor says an even clumsier maid hasn't noticed her coworker died.

A ship that lost its master to storms or pirates and became undead after long years adrift. It takes in shipwreck victims and attacks merchant ships to gain crew. An old charm against it was to "greet the sea," though now and then an Echo answered.

An odd spirit with a tube-shaped body whose end crosses into itself. Follow its outside with your eyes and you're inside; follow the inside and you're back outside. Normal to higher-dimensional beings, but if we try to grasp it, at worst we go mad.
The ghost of a hunter who grew so absorbed in the hunt that they forgot to eat and starved to death in the forest. The will to keep hunting even after death seems to have become this ghost.

The ghost of a female brawler bitterly defeated and killed in a duel. Her body lost, but her soul did not. To prove that her fists are the strongest of all, she challenges adventurers to duels to the death.

When a Valkyrie dies, her god normally calls her soul to its rightful place. But some, rejected for deeds in life like breaking commandments, wander with nowhere to go. A weak heart seeks a god's salvation, and is rejected for that weakness. How sad.

An evil spirit that startles adventurers with strange faces and screams. Once you flinch and your guard drops, it devours your soul. They say the way to drive it off is to strike the same pose and scream back.

A skull that swims through the air like a ray. Usually it glides lazily just above the ground, like a ray in the sea, but once it spots prey, it closes in on your feet at terrifying speed without a sound, then leaps up to strike all at once.

In a land far to the east, the leader of the samurai is called a Daimyo. This samurai is a Daimyo who wanders the world even in death. Having lost a war and his domain, he attacks any adventurer he comes across, seeking to win his lands back.

The ghost of a ninja who rose to the rank of Summer, only to lose their life. Less deadly than in life, yet it still hides killing skill not to be taken lightly. If you think you can't win, ask it nicely to pass on to heaven.

A vengeful dog spirit made by the curse kodoku. Inugami are said to be passed down in certain bloodlines for generations, often cited as proof that ordinary people, animals and plants can be drawn into dark arts. How sad, to find no freedom even in death.

Spirit energy gathered and given form. The area around it becomes a special field, where overflowing spirit energy crystallizes. The mist-like stuff drifting about can also become arms that crush foes at Mayokal's will.

King of the evil spirits. At this level, it no longer lingers in this world because it is lost, but by its own will. Spirits are everywhere, many of them souls with nowhere to go. The king summons such spirits as servants, making its position rock solid.
The lowest class of demon. Even so, it has more than enough power to kill novice adventurers. It moves fast and strikes twice, with fangs and claws.
A demon's arm sprouting from the ground. No one knows what lies at the other end.
A cruel little demon. Alone it is a coward, but in a group it seems to grow bold and turns vicious. Watch out when a group of them attacks.

One who walks the night. If you sense strange footsteps behind you in the dark, it may be a Night Stalker. Give it an opening, and in an instant you'll be dragged into the darkness and become Night Stalkers yourselves.

A lesser demon. Low-ranking, yet it calls its friends and attacks, so it's dangerous unless you wipe them out quickly. It may be good practice for intermediate adventurers, but don't let your guard down.
A crafty, learned demon. It chants spells in a hoarse voice. Leave it alone and it becomes a nuisance, so let's ask Grandpa to retire early.
It looks like a smiling bishop, but its true body is the eerily glowing hand behind it. Any adventurer fooled into coming close will be caught in the blink of an eye.

A female knight who lives in darkness. One thrust of her matchless spear sends frail spellcasters to the grave. 'Valkyrie' means a battle maiden blessed by the gods, yet she is a demon Valkyrie. If even demons serve a god, what kind of being is their god?

A male dream demon flaunting a lewd symbol. Incubi would rather violate the mind with words than the body, digging up the desires prey can tell no one. Once in their arms, normal acts never satisfy you; you roam unfulfilled, devouring body after body.

A demon who leads adventurers astray with her bewitching form. Even veterans can't handle the Succubus, in more ways than one. Her level drain is a menace. And yet... having your hard-won experience sucked away in sweet dreams... isn't that a fine life?

A higher demon than the Lesser Demon. It keeps the habit of calling its friends, but with greater physical strength and magic. It is fairly tough too, so it's dangerous unless you finish it off in one go.

A demon posing as an angel. He is kind at first to those who come seeking salvation, but once they are of no use, he steals their souls with a burst of laughter. Watching their faces as absolute peace of mind turns to despair is his greatest pleasure.

A demon in a pitiful state. Why it suffers so is unknown, but it is said it was reduced to this form after losing a power struggle among the Demon Dukes. Bound and unable to speak, it can still freeze your heart with muffled roars and a piercing glare.
Hell's jailer, who rules demons with the whip in hand. For a lesser demon, defying him means death. In battle he seldom dirties his own hands, preferring to summon his minions to do the attacking.

A savage she-demon smashing all with great claws. Famed for cruelty, she torments lovely prey hardest till it breaks. Ramming claws down the throats of pleading prey to force gags, peering at faces warped by terror, wet with tears and snot: her routine.

A copper-skinned greater demon. Its name means "calamity" and "evil," and it is said to hold every wicked thought. Its malice is so pure that even if you win, your heart will be deeply wounded. The wound festers, and one day you become the next Fiend.

A demon embodying the underworld's flames. It holds 1,024 legions and leads Demon Valkyries and Hell Masters. Unusually for a demon, it wields priest spells calling down divine miracles. If the gods guarantee our justice, who proves the gods' justice?

A monstrous woman whose gaze turns onlookers to stone with terror. Not only her petrifying spells but her normal attacks are fierce. Few have seen her, but they say that when she laid down her arms, her eyes held a sorrow, as if longing for days gone by.

A monster that rules the world of darkness alongside the Vampire Lord, the twin pillars of that realm. They say the Fiend King's blow shatters any holy armor, and the magic it unleashes blasts away any divine grace.
A small flying dragon, the most commonly seen kind. But it is not weak. Take it lightly, and the gale from its wings will blow you away.
A dragon covered in copper scales. Unlike a Wyvern, it plants both feet on the ground to attack. It is probably the first truly dragon-like dragon you will meet.

A green-bodied dragon. It lives in caves and high mountains and swoops down to the lands below for food. Even if Wyverns and Copper Dragons make you think you're used to dragons, a Green Dragon will teach you their terror all over again.

A two-headed dragon whose tail is also a head. Strong against attacks from all sides, it assails adventurers with balanced offense and defense. The two heads get along well. Coiled up asleep with both heads side by side, it is surprisingly adorable.

A dragon covered in red skin, also known as the lava dragon. It can breathe hellfire without end. It is one of the stronger dragons known. When you fight it, block the breath or fortify your front line with fire-resistant gear.

Poison coats it from fang to claw tip. Even a scratch will make you double over, but scarier still is its venomous breath. Weaker than other elemental breaths, it causes status ailments. If you meet one, hit it fast and wear it down.
A many-headed great serpent. Its breath aside, its number of attacks is staggering. Unless you pin it down well with single-target spells and such, it will steadily wear down your party's HP.

A dragon that hates having its back seen or being taken from behind. But it moves so sluggishly that it is always sad. All a Grannada can do is turn its head and glare bitterly with its one eye. The wistful nursery rhyme 'Behind the Grannada' is famous.
A dragon born of rainbow light. It swims through light, and when it mingles with clouds, it rains seven-colored diamond dust upon the land. Though a dragon, it is closer to a spirit or ghost.

A great dragon that 'swims' through the earth, burrowing into bedrock. Rarely seen, and unlike other dragons, little is known of its habits. Among adventurers there is talk that 'it may not be a dragon at all,' but its roots remain uncertain.

A two-headed dragon. It can fly, but usually it slithers over the ground like a snake. Its sight, smell and hearing are keen, so once it targets you, escape is no easy matter. Out of respect for its strength, it is often depicted on emblems.

A golden dragon clad in the power of lightning. Highly intelligent, it rarely attacks without warning, but once battle begins it will treat you to the full course of dragon terror, breath and claws alike. Even the Kin of Darkness are wary of it.

A wyvern holding the power of the earth. From its body, blessed by the spirits, it breathes holy breath. The Elemental Wieg is said to appear when harmony among those who live on that land is disturbed.

A mighty wyvern clutching a natural emerald. Its magic is superb too: besides dragon attacks, it deftly showers foes with magic light amplified by the emerald. It prefers emeralds but may take diamonds or rubies. Some are seen fighting over one emerald.

Revered by dragonkind as the 'Mother of Dragons' and the 'Dragon Queen.' She alone in this world knows true strength and beauty. She never forgives those who harm her kin; no one who has incurred her wrath has ever survived.

Drifters who have lost their pride and goals and make a living just by attacking adventurers. In a sense, they're nastier than Thieves. For now, let's have them serve as stepping stones toward our own goals.

A samurai with no master. Origins vary: some lost their lord, others roamed alone as they pleased from the start. Wanderers they may be, but their skill is real. Take them lightly and you'll become "rust on the katana," or whatever it is they call it.

An elf swordsman, most often in Isfald's service. Elves make up for their lack of brawn with disciplined strategy and tactics, and so crush warriors of other races who scatter and act tough. Then again, pick them off one by one and they fall easily.

A warrior swallowed up by the feel of blood and flesh in battle. It rampages with tremendous strength and physical prowess, but there is no need to meet it head-on. Put it to sleep with a spell or the like.

A swordsman baptized after swearing to fight for the gods. They kill and destroy for their doctrine, but with the gods' teachings, they never need to doubt or agonize. Only they know the worth of the 'peace of mind' they gave up their own lives to gain.

Warriors who train their bodies to the limit and crush foes with their own strength. Their fighting ability is truly remarkable. Their well-built muscles seem a point of pride; if they're friendly, they'll show off their physique without holding back.

A warrior fused with a chariot by alchemy. It turns tighter than it looks, and a head-on charge is hard to take well. Nor is fleeing easy: escape onto mountain trails or other unpaved roads, and it swaps its wheels for spiked ones and gives chase.

A vicious warrior who appears with dash and flair to the brisk sound of galloping, then attacks. Like some ball game, it swings its hammer to knock adventurers' heads clean off. A small few of these warriors even dream of fighting on horseback.

An avenger: one who exacts revenge. Broadly it is not limited to warriors, but usually means those who wield the sword for vengeance. They may have their own creed, but you have no reason to die for their satisfaction. Fight fair and drive them off.

A samurai who has gained superior ability and leadership. At this rank they apparently come to hold lands of their own. They seem to enjoy having plenty of party members, and are often seen parading about in large groups.

A Lord fallen into the world of darkness. But even a rotten Lord is still a Lord. Its sword strokes flow without falter, showing the chivalry of darkness. With strong defense and mighty blows, it will surely drive you into a corner.

Royals clad in unfamiliar garb. Hedonists who think anything goes if it's fun, they burst into song and dance for no reason at all. Their mustache is their charm point; lose it and they can't bounce back for a while. In other words, go for the mustache.

A female fighter who dearly loves to fight. Taking no lover, she sates every desire by driving her fists into others' bodies. Her whole body is a weapon; she excels at close combat. Want to writhe in agony from her passionate gut blow? Charge right in.

A samurai with the honored duty of raising the war banner, the army's symbol, in battle. In peacetime they also advise on domestic affairs, so are rather intellectual. Perhaps from handling the real work, their skill reportedly beats their lord's at times.

A lord of a land far east, on a stacked cushion called a 'zabutoon.' This lord crushes foes with political clout, not brawn, and lewdly calls women over when possible. Sweets set on gold coins somehow delight this lord, so bring some to get friendly.
A Lord of the dragonewts. The ultimate warrior, uniting the power of dragons, magic, and the spirit of a king. It meets every foe with sword, spells and breath.

A samurai who has mastered the finest skills. In a master's hands even a nameless katana is deadly. Disarm it, and a lightning-fast dagger still slashes you deep in the side. A living legend of many tales. If you face it, show what today's living can do.

A mage who has just learned spells. All they can do yet is cast fireballs or put you to sleep, but because their attack pattern never changes, adventurers who fall for it fall hard. Better safe than sorry.

Alchemy is often thought of as research into making gold, but refining gold is only one of its results. The alchemists' aim is to unlock the laws of this world and make all things more perfect. The Philosopher's Stone exists as the medium for that.
The doors of Rubenburg are open to all. Graduating, however, is no easy matter. Can you hold on to what you feel now, full of dreams and hope, until the very end?

Students gather from all over, so their everyday clothes vary too. The school issues uniforms, but on days off everyone returns to their homeland's customs, and the school buildings apparently turn into a kind of international fashion show.
A woman trained in sorcery. She knows her spells better than a Mage does, so stay on your guard.
A tarot card user who draws fate in with great power. Depending on the situation, a tarot card may plunge you into unexpected danger. Better to defeat them before they get out of hand.

They do study, sort of, but now that they're used to student life, they tend to slack in all sorts of ways. All they've gotten good at is dodging problems and fudging things; no real skill to show. A dangerous age, when temptation easily leads one astray.

Schoolgirls who studied hard and can now handle quite a few spells. Compared to boys their age, they're more grown in body and mind. Once they learn how to wrap men around their fingers, they'll make fine High Sorceresses.

Sorceresses among the Witches who mastered higher magic through further training. Maybe everyone gets this way with room to breathe, but High Sorceresses are generally refined. Leading junior Witches, they giggle as they toy with adventurers using magic.

Wielders of more advanced alchemy, with a wider range of spells. At the intermediate level of alchemy, they begin to take an interest in 'the birth of life' as research. Creating life is dogged by 'bioethics,' but will that ever reach their ears?

A witch's pet snail that escaped and gained wisdom. Alas, poor snail, its speed is just what you'd expect. But on top of a sorcerer's gifts, it has hard defense and decent stamina. Don't play 'Snail, snail, where are your eyes?' -- just defeat it quickly.

An alchemist out gathering materials while enjoying a carefree picnic. Gentle by nature, finding small joys in meeting people on the road. But adventurers alone seem to stir up mixed feelings, and on meeting one, the Picnicker flees at full speed.

Third-years about to graduate, writhing in a storm of remedial classes. The school values tradition and pride, so without real skill you're soon held back. Some fake it with magic, but teachers usually see through it and hold them back. Plan your studies.

Third-years about to graduate. Afterward, some will join the palace Magic Bureau, some will aid small farm villages as mages, others will seek deeper knowledge. What kind of mages will they become as they leave the nest? May happiness be theirs.

A fearsome mage who has learned every Mage spell. Naturally, they cast the strongest attack spells. They expect foes to target them first, so they always have a spell ready to go. If they spot a Kannagi among the foes, they pull a very sour face.

One who has completed the full course of alchemical study. She has even created the artificial life 'Homunculus'; all that remains is the Philosopher's Stone. People with a goal seem full of life, and this old woman is no exception: she looks very spry.

A noisy bard who blares away on an instrument called the bagpipe. With a bellows-like air bag, a tune can be played without a break. But handling it takes real stamina, so by the time you can play it freely, you may have become a muscle-bound spellcaster.
One who has trained as a Summoner and grown strong enough to bury an average adventurer single-handed. They summon one creature after another, as if building a wall of monsters.

A mage of unknown identity in a clown's guise. It loves death and decadent games, and once its curiosity is sated, it gives a shrill, strange laugh. All wonder at its true face; none has seen it. Popping in and out of nowhere, it may not even be human.

A priestess directly under Sarijana, goddess of growth and carnal love. Her body, which enthralls man and woman alike, is a divine gift. But every rose has thorns. Master of Tarot, nuclear magic and barriers, she'll send you to heaven, body and soul.
Not a few priests turn to evil alignments or seek to serve dark gods. Some Priest spells are frightening, but at this level, you can safely treat them as a not-very-good Fighter.

A novice maid with a bucket and a deck brush. Maybe because she is new, she makes blunder after blunder. She is hard to dislike, but you can still get hurt in the fallout, so you had better be careful.

Casts both Priest and Mage spells, but at this level, there is nothing much to worry about. Among foes of similar rank, Priests and Mages are scarier than Bishops. Don't let the title fool you into choosing the wrong target first.

A battle maiden blessed by the gods and versed in the spear. With keen insight she reads her foes' moves and cuts them down with blinding speed. Her spear reaches even the back row. Be careful if you ever have to fight one.

A female priest who lives by an alignment unlike ours. Take her lightly and you will get hurt. Yet one question remains. Any priest must worship some god, but plainly not one of the six. So who lends her power?

A maid now trusted with key duties such as hosting guests. Tray of tea things in hand, hand on her hip, she exudes confidence in her work. Why not order something if you feel like it? You will pay with your life.

Traveling with adventurers, this one now fights better than a proper bishop. Still, a bishop is a bishop, so some dubious preaching goes on too. After thrashing foes with spells comes the fun, fun sermon time.

A priest who travels spreading the gods' teachings. So strong is their faith that at some point they learned to fly. When they find prey, they creep up without a sound, surround it with their comrades, and start talking about love.

A man who rings a bell to celebrate adventurers' departure for the next world. He must really love ringing it: he rings away with a broad (creepy) grin. And though it is very rare, in the dark world people have reportedly had him officiate real ceremonies.

A shrine priest from a land far to the east. With strange paper and sticks, they fight undead monsters, spirits among them. But as foes, fear their 'Barrier': it reflects most spells, so a party that relies solely on spells will struggle.

One who has reached the highest level of power among priests. A priest's true calling is healing and comfort, but in battle they use instant-death spells. To them, granting death is also a kind of mercy. That mercy, of course, we would rather decline.

Head maid of the labyrinth. With calm judgment and precise action, she meets her master's every wish; her planner holds their full schedule. Leave it to her and all is well, but she's inflexible, hence strict. In battle, her fierce kicks crush their foes.

'Master Bishop' has two meanings. One is master by trade, trusted with a church; the other is master as an adventurer grown as strong as one can get. It may be none of our business, but for a bishop, which life is more worthwhile?

An eastern Kannagi or Summoner, retained by royal houses and shoguns for prophecy, sorcery and divination. They usually perform all manner of rites, but when they sense a spirit, they command monsters called "Shiki" to drive the evil away.

A battle maiden who mastered her path, she skewers foes on a holy spear as the gods teach. Stricter than Valkyries, she hates impurity of body and above all of soul: heart and faith. Such zeal may look comical, but have you found a faith that strong?

The strongest, most evil pontiff, who cast off self and gave his soul to evil. He asked his god to enslave his soul; his self is nearly gone, his deeds bound by doctrine. Never doubting, he seems a puppet. Perhaps this is a form of 'ultimate happiness.'
A thief after adventurers' belongings. With a full party, they are not much of a problem. Leave them alone and they will run off on their own.
Deep in the forest, rangers stalk live animals nearly every day. Their focus and patience on the hunt are formidable, so if poison or paralysis slows you down, be prepared for the worst.
The lowest rank of ninja. Being a novice, its moves are still clumsy. At worst, a Fighter or Mage of the same level may even be stronger, but it does still have a small chance to decapitate.

A villain who prowls the labyrinth, using the dirty trick of ganging up on weakened adventurers. Individually, though, they are not very strong, so if you make full use of magic and the like, you should be able to fight them fairly safely.

A warden of the forest, merciless to any who despoil it. A famous Forest Guard is Polyte, though she is a woman. Her tale became the play 'Periatif'. The scene in which she, in tears, shoots the lover who broke the forest's law is unforgettable once seen.

A female ninja drilled in shinobi skills and mindset. She uses her womanhood as a weapon, so underestimate her and you'll pay. Stand beside her and you'll notice a faint, sweet scent at her collar. One of the few vanities a kunoichi is allowed?

A bold way of life, and the strong luck to back it up. A thief with both is called a Lucky Star. They are skilled enough to found a band of thieves of their own, and their varied fighting styles are sure to throw adventurers into a panic.

A Blob that learned to use a bow. Human types have only two arms, but these have many tentacles, so when each one draws a bow and they fire in volleys, they are a handful. Luckily, their aim is poor, so stay calm and seize your chance to win.

It appears at night and downs prey in the dark. Its aim earned it the name of one who shoots down the moon. In 'Periatif,' it is Jenas, Polyte's rival. The scene of their arrows colliding over the moon on the lake, sparks flying, has even been painted.

A ninja with even more training. Attack, agility, decapitation rate and many other abilities have all risen. If you meet one, do not leave it be: take it down. By the time your head has left your body, it is too late.

Some people just have sticky fingers: they pick pockets with no real need, or steal for fun. A Beauty lulls you with her looks and walks off with your valuables. And should she be found out, one stab of a hidden knife settles it.

A kunoichi who could no longer hold back her wish to show off her beauty to all. Other kunoichi scorn them as heretics, but such words don't reach these wild girls. Kunoichi arts honed even further--can you weather them?

A werebeast's special ability lets normal attacks carry poison, and a werebeast Ranger can follow up on itself. An Arc Launcher, being a werebeast, is a dire threat to parties with no poison resistance.
A ninja holding the title of Summer. Don't underestimate it just because it is alone. Once it hides, you cannot touch it, and one by one your heads will be lopped off.
A small, imp-like race common on the continent. Being small, they are not much of a threat even when they attack by force. Just brush them off.
A race akin to the werebeasts, but more savage than the other races. They have their own culture and territory, and outside battle they have no contact with humans or elves.

Like kobolds, a race akin to the werebeasts. With big appetites, they know 512 kinds of junk food, likely the fruit of chasing their own idea of fine food. The orc king is chosen by this gourmet score: the one who lets everyone eat better is truly king.

A beastfolk girl with skunk blood. Maybe it's her skunk nature, but when worked up, she gasses. When angry, of course, but also happy or sad; any feeling sets her off. So she is shunned, friendless and lonely. And then, feeling lonely, she gasses again.

A spider-like enchantress. Near her rear she spins sticky thread to snare prey, hard to cut and hard to escape. But she has a weak spot: thrust an arm into the spinneret and rip out the thread's source to wear Taranti down. Not that she'll let you easily.

Among beastfolk and demi-humans, the Ogre has the most commanding presence. Good at swinging axes and hammers, it has the most muscular body of all beastfolk. However sturdy your shield, it can hit you right through it. It often hangs out with goblins.

A demi-human monster that evolved in an unusual way. With partisan in hand it spears fish, and adventurers. It hates dryness and prefers to live in wetlands. The orcs recently taught them about seasonings, and salt-grilled fish is now all the rage.

A swift half-horse beastfolk archer that hunts in packs. Its hunts usually succeed, but it is also known for lechery, carrying off adventurers stunned by poison arrows on its back to wed them. Not just women: handsome men get taken too. Such barbarians.

By kobold custom the strongest becomes King, decided by nothing less than a clan-wide brawl. Young and old, men and women all pile in, so a female King sometimes emerges. Hence most past Kings are hotheads. Only Kings may wear a red cape.

The gourmet king who reigns over orc society. Perhaps eating well really does make you stronger, for the Orc King has abilities worthy of the title. Take it lightly and you will end up as their dinner.

The leader of the lizardmen. It is bigger built and more athletic than an ordinary lizardman, and no easy opponent. As befits a king, its hunting skill is beyond doubt: it can spear three fish with a single thrust.

A beautiful monster, human above and fish below. Trespass in their waters and they come in groups to drive you out. For all their aggression, they are said to be keenly interested in romance. When they drive off a gentleman, they sigh among the waves.
A guard of the Ogre Lord. A trained ogre, it acts with discipline, for an ogre. When ogre brawn and goblin spells attack together, they become tough foes.

A cute-looking beastfolk girl who hunts those who stray into the woods. Ask her in turn, "Why are your hands so hairy?" "Why do your eyes gleam so?" "Why are there fangs in your mouth?" She answers politely, edging closer step by step with a hidden knife.

A girl born to a tiger and a human, who thinks she's a tiger. Get near with ulterior motives and she'll surely bite, taking you for food. Catlike, she rubs her face very hard before rain. But go near thinking 'Aww, cute!' and you'll still be eaten.

A Goblin whose talent for magic has blossomed. It knows both fire and ice spells, a nuisance when it hangs back. Then again, drag it to the front or poke it with long-reach weapons, and it is no problem at all.

Queen of the mermaids, ruler of the sea. In hand she holds a special spear, the 'Holy Sea Trident,' and strikes intruders with lightning. She usually sits deep in the sea, but on calm full-moon nights she leads the mermaids to the surface for a feast.

A dread lord who has lost reason and swings his sword at friend and foe. No longer human, he is a mad beast. Yet by chance even a Raver Lord may regain his senses. Then, unable to bear his sins, he tries to destroy himself... dragging those near along.
A giant living in the forest. Not evil, but if you approach, it will usually shoo you away as a nuisance, or attack. If you are unlucky enough to fight it, try using wits, not strength.
A strange giant with two heads growing from its neck. Violent by nature, it constantly scans its surroundings with both heads. The two heads often quarrel over which one controls the body.

Bull-headed, closer to a monster than a giant. One tale says a noblewoman pined for a young, sturdy bull, and through a cursed act she conceived and bore this monster. Its body is human, but it attacks with a bull's wits and ferocity.

A giant of fire that lives on flames. It prefers natural fire to man-made or spell-made flame. Old friends with Frost Giants. Them being together seems bad, but they are not Elementals, so it's fine. Shaking hands, singing arm in arm: no sweat.

A one-eyed giant gifted at smithing, of an odd race whose every member can do smithing and alchemy. Gruff like most craftsmen, but mild-natured. They like to live near volcanoes, where fire is always at hand. Visit one and it may sell you a special weapon.

An ice giant. It favors the 'Freezing Sword,' which freezes what it touches, and likes to freeze foes and then shatter them. It sometimes brings seafood to the Fire Giants, who grill it piping hot at once. Inwardly it sighs: 'Raw tastes better...'

A giant with three faces. The top one thinks, the second moves the arms, the third the legs. Cheerful, it befriends anyone, but after a while its pushy nature starts to show. In a good mood, it can be seen racing over hills and fields with a booming laugh.

A giant girl who lives in the sea. Despite her huge body, she is shy and bashful. When a tsunami she caused by moving heads for ships or fishing villages, she frets it will take small lives (which makes more tsunamis). Her dream is to be a lovely bride.

A giant cloaked in toxins. One theory says life evolves in many ways in many environments. Did this giant evolve this way to survive in toxic lands? Either way, it became a vicious giant whose very breath inflicts deadly poison.

A wounded giant was treated by a passing priest and, deeply moved, began training as a priest too: the Cosplay Priest. But not knowing how to train, it just swings a club while shouting spell names it picked up. Someone should guide it, don't you think?

A giant shrouded in mystery. Mages and alchemists say it is a constructed giant; Summoners say it is a monster called from another world. Either way, it is surely one of the more troublesome foes adventurers face. Care to solve its mystery yourselves?

Once a female spirit ruling the sky, she grew close to a wind spirit and made the other spirits jealous. As a result, she was dragged from the sky to the ground. Her longing for the sky remains, but now she drifts over the land as one of the wind spirits.

The god of life-creation, who presides over the birth of life. Ildraha has a fiery, rash side. New life is ever trying to well up from within Ildraha's body, held back only by a seal Ildraha has placed on it.

The god of pleasure and change, who presides over the growth of life. Ashtel is Naru's older sister; the two are sister gods. A hedonist who loves uproar and chaos, she acts on likes and dislikes like a child and makes Naru clean up her messes.
The god of death, who presides over the end of life. A quiet god who watches the life and death of the world with a detached gaze, and whose body goes on receiving the 'death' of every living thing.

The god of space, who makes from nothing the space to build worlds in, and chief of the six gods. Clever but extremely pedantic, Void cannot stand anything not going exactly to design, and so resents Ildraha, who acts purely on emotion.

The god of time, who brings the flow of time to the world, and Ashtel's younger sister. Naru holds an 'hourglass' called 'Tonak-Kanakol.' Void and the others must find the 'Eld' before it runs out; if they fail, the realm of the gods is said to collapse.

The god of existence, who affirms that each thing 'is' there. Without Dehain's approval, no created thing can ever exist in the world. Whether something once approved can be 'revoked,' Dehain has never tried, and so does not know.

The former god of life-creation, loving all life alike. Running for chief god to make a life paradise and the Eld, Orses won no support, clashing with Dehain. Torn by duty and heart, Orses chose heart, left hopes to an heir, and went to the event horizon.

The former god of change, a goddess who dozes often and acts on dreams. One day she dreamed the gods' world fell, and grieved for life left wailing in the chaos. Keener on rebuilding order after the fall than on the stalled Eld, she made a certain factor.

The former god of space, managing space as Void does now. A god of laughter too, Semnadoc did all sorts to cheer Dehain, tormented by regret over the Urna affair. For a certain reason, Semnadoc abdicated by choice: rare, barring dismissal or no-confidence.

The former god of time. The gods in the Creation Womb Palace are the six creation gods of Urna's birth. Of the living gods, Sinhanicol was among the closest to the birth of "Tonak-Kanakol," and is a mystery. Sinhanicol then awaited a calm, impartial heir.

'A shield in my right hand, and in my left, a shield too! ...Huh?' At a cave mouth stands a statue of a boy who carelessly equipped two shields in battle and died. At some point, the statue began to spar with anyone who talks to it, even while dozing off.

An elder heading the Bistel Magic Bureau, who with its staff bars monsters with a spell barrier on the walls. Archelon's granddaughter fell for an adventurer and rarely visits, hence the foul mood. Is that why Archelon is hard on adventurers in the cave?

Noble dragonkind is a race apart. Proud of their neutrality, dragons shun humans and elves and should never side with the Kin of Darkness. But his forebears grew close to them, so like the Dragonfolk he is disowned by dragonkind and must live in darkness.

A monstrous woman serving Demon Duke Animacie. Her swift attacks from her bizarre body are unpredictable. By Espel-Dex's contract she was told to aid Zeshrom, and so joined this fight. Her aim: a cure for her master's ailing body.
A spectral warrior. A member of Espel-Dex, Nonhared has destroyed land after land. Zeshrom is Nonhared's direct superior, but Nonhared is not happy with the way he works.

A hedonist living for fun with no wish to serve. None at all. Liking it here, the Mistress got a divine relic, kept mum and settled in the pleasure district. The Mistress taught a Demon Duke's daughter bad ways and, having lost touch, frets like a bad pal.

A devil of Espel-Dex. Having found a special Zefkaka, he plots to seize its power and expand Espel-Dex. A master schemer but a bit soft-hearted, he has little taste for pure destruction. His ideal is smart yet aggressive rule, and he strives for it daily.

An ancient evil spirit trying to take this land. Fiona's name was carved on the Holy Foundation, Contrachio, symbol of sovereignty over the land, but she has rewritten it with her own name to make this land hers.

The land of Zeshrom's birth was on the brink of being scrapped. To escape that, its Zefkaka set out to reset itself, cast out the life rooted in it, Zeshrom included, and rose again as a New Land. Cast off by his own land, how does Zeshrom see Urna?

A Zefkaka is a land's soul or will. All Zefkaka are said to have split off from the first fragment, the Primordial Soil, and grown into lands. By an old twist of fate, this land held both Fiona's and Urna's Zefkaka. Now, which Zefkaka will you choose?

Urna, lawful sovereign of the land via the divine relics. Its life should have hailed her return, but the wall of time made it unwelcome. Fiona, who once took the New Land's rights from her, blocks her again, and in sorrow Urna swings the Sword of Wrath.
One of the Four Sages of the Hestrio Continent: a giant owl who rules the wind. Possessed of much ancient wisdom, it is said to be the closest of the Four Sages to humans.

One of the Four Sages of the Hestrio Continent: a giant dog who rules fire. Fierce by nature, he lives in the Scorching Castle with the creatures who adore him. He rules fire but is no fire spirit, so when it gets too hot, he snaps.

One of the Four Sages of the Hestrio Continent: a giant jellyfish who rules water. Her coral crown lets her know the state of the whole sea. She loves quiet, and cannot stand the hot-blooded or the noisy.

One of the Four Sages of the Hestrio Continent: a giant mole who rules the earth. Raizam lived in the Blanc Desert but somehow never felt at home there, and wants to move away. Not very bright, but the most sensible of the Four Sages.

Leaving the Princess's land, a strange light felled us into ages of sleep. Awake, we forgot the past and guarded folk here, till a dear voice called from below!? We answer her now! I am Omsis of Wind!! "Come, Princess! Let's finish our broken dream!"

Leaving the Princess's land, a strange light felled us into ages of sleep. Awake, we forgot the past and guarded folk here, till a dear voice called from below!? We answer her now! I am Rades of Fire!! "We kept 'em safe! You'll praise us, right, Princess?"

Leaving the Princess's land, a strange light felled us into ages of sleep. Awake, we forgot the past and guarded folk here, till a dear voice called from below!? We answer her now! I am Shirins of Water!! "Oh Princess, this time I'll stay to the end!!"
